data.description:
## Description
**What**: Wire the published contract into its three consumers: (a) plugins/dso/hooks/pre-commit-intent-coverage-gate.sh, (b) 94ed-f55c's manifest-aware default validator finding-type mapping, (c) .github/workflows/intent-coverage.yml.
**Why**: A finding that no surface consumes is invisible; this story delivers the multi-surface consumption that makes closure non-silent and gives CI a per-PR signal.
**Scope**:
- IN: pre-commit-intent-coverage-gate.sh invoking only the FAST checks (file existence plus header parse) with no test-runner invocation, block-mode reserved for intent_with_no_test at closure-time detected via the ticket-transition hook; the 94ed validator ingesting findings JSON and registering all seven finding types for rendering in the completion-verifier 'Intent Allocation Findings' section; intent-coverage.yml invoking both scripts plus the step-iii test-pass validation at CI time, posting findings via upsert-by-marker on the stable marker COVERAGE_FINDINGS_<epic-id>, with a GHA-job-summary fallback when comment-write is unavailable.
- OUT: the scripts themselves (sc-2, sc-3); the e2e fixture suite (sc-5); per-language dynamic-import detection (sc-6).

## Done Definitions

- pre-commit-intent-coverage-gate.sh invokes only file-existence and header-parse checks (no test runner) and does not block on warn-only findings ← Satisfies: sc-4
- pre-commit-intent-coverage-gate.sh validates the findings JSON it ingests against the sc-1 jsonschema before processing and skips malformed findings ← Satisfies: sc-1
- The 94ed manifest-aware validator ingests the findings JSON, validates it against the sc-1 schema, and registers all seven finding types for rendering; a closure with an unregistered SC produces a non-empty 'Intent Allocation Findings' section naming the SC ← Validates Closure Check: "(i) MID_SPRINT_SC_ADDITION: fixture epic with 1 SC and 1 test_artifact registered passing; a 2nd SC is added to the epic description without registering a corresponding test_artifact. intent-coverage-check.sh surfaces intent_with_no_test for the new SC; completion-verifier dispatch produces non-empty 'Intent Allocation Findings' section. Verifies the primary real-world miss pattern."
- intent-coverage.yml validates the findings JSON produced by both scripts against the sc-1 jsonschema before posting the PR comment or GHA summary, rejecting malformed findings ← Satisfies: sc-1
- The closure-time block-check reads the manifest deferred_test field and does not block closure for an intent whose entry sets deferred_test:true ← Satisfies: sc-4
- intent-coverage.yml invokes both scripts plus the step-iii test-pass validation and upserts a single PR comment by the COVERAGE_FINDINGS_<epic-id> marker, editing in place on re-run rather than threading ← Satisfies: sc-4
- When comment-write is unavailable the workflow writes the findings to the GHA job summary so the marker and findings are not dropped ← Satisfies: sc-4
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic ← Satisfies: sc-4

## Considerations

- [Dependency] External blocker a03c-d55e-1393-4f27: the 94ed validator is registered with a03c's pluggable end-state-item-validator hook.
- [Dependency] External blocker 94ed-f55c-51f5-45f6: consumer (b) hooks into 94ed's manifest-aware default validator.
- [Build] pre-commit-intent-coverage-gate.sh is a new .sh file and must have its executable bit set per CLAUDE.md.
- [Deployment] On fork PRs with a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN the comment upsert fails; the GHA-summary fallback is the interim signal pending fork-PR security work.
- [Scope/Ownership] This story owns the closure-time intent_with_no_test block-check wiring (via the ticket-transition hook) plus its deferred_test:true suppression (epic State Lifecycle: SC4(a) pre-commit gate plus closure-time block-check is the CONSUME owner of deferred_test). draft-4 scenario (f) only exercises suppression as a fixture; the consuming logic is built here.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a sprint orchestrator, I want the findings consumed across pre-commit, the 94ed validator, and CI, so that coverage gaps surface at the right surface with the right severity.
